nodes.title: Bitcoin Custody
nodes.body:
**Educational presentation — not financial advice.**

Explore how people hold Bitcoin keys through interactive decisions.
Your path accumulates in the trail. **Risks** and **hardening** stack as you go.

Open **Paths** for a curated walkthrough, or explore freely from the custody ladder.

nodes.title: What is custody?
nodes.body:
**Custody** means who can authorize spending your Bitcoin.

- If an exchange holds the keys, **they** custody your coins (you hold an IOU).
- If you hold the seed/private keys, **you** custody them (self-custody).
- Hybrids exist: federations, multisig co-signers, collaborative custody.

*Not your keys, not your coins* — but self-custody also means *your keys, your responsibility*.

nodes.title: The custody ladder
nodes.body:
Climb from maximum convenience and counterparty trust toward maximum sovereignty and operational burden:

1. **Custodian** (exchange)
2. **Federation**
3. **Single-key hot wallet**
4. **Single-key hardware wallet**
5. **Air-gapped / cold storage**
6. **Multisignature**
7. **Distributed multisig**
8. **Multisig with independent parties**
9. **High-security protocols** (e.g. Glacier-style)

Each rung trades day-to-day ease and recoverability against security and operational burden.
Pick a rung to dive in — or open **Paths** for a curated walkthrough.

choices.label: Deep dive: generating a seed phrase

nodes.title: Custodian (exchange / hosted wallet)
nodes.body:
A company holds Bitcoin on your behalf. You log in with **username/password** and usually **2FA**.

**Benefits**
- Exchange trading, fiat on/off ramps
- Lightning payments (often)
- Recovery via identity verification / support
- Withdrawal limits, some inheritance/beneficiary policies

**You can be phished.** You hold an account, not necessarily on-chain keys.

nodes.title: Custodian — benefits
nodes.body:
- **Exchange services**: spot, often derivatives; easy fiat rails
- **Lightning**: many custodians offer LN without channel management
- **Auth model**: password + email/OTP 2FA (upgrade to hardware 2FA!)
- **Recovery**: KYC / support can reset access if you lose credentials (unlike seed loss)
- **Withdrawal limits**: can slow attackers who get into your account
- **Inheritance policies**: some offer beneficiary designation (varies; legal complexity remains)

Tradeoff: convenience and institutional recovery come with **counterparty** and **privacy** risk.

nodes.title: Custodian — risks & loss of funds
nodes.body:
**Loss of funds**
- Debasement / fractional reserves (IOU risk)
- Seizure (government or civil)
- Hacks of hot wallets / infrastructure
- Insider theft
- Insolvency / bankruptcy → creditors ahead of you

**Loss of funds or privacy**
- Rogue employees, database breaches
- Police / legal process against the custodian

**Access & social attacks**
- Phishing, social engineering
- SIM-swap against SMS 2FA
- Compromised credentials
- Withdrawal / account freezes

nodes.title: Custodian — mitigations
nodes.body:
Natural mitigations (still not eliminating counterparty risk):

- **Hardware 2FA** (security keys) — defeat most SIM-swaps
- **Withdrawal allowlists** + delay on allowlist changes
- **Split holdings** — only working capital on exchanges
- **Proof-of-reserves** awareness (limited assurance)
- **Periodic withdrawals** to wallets you control
- Unique passwords; never enter creds on links from email/DM

nodes.title: Hardened custodial posture
nodes.body:
You've reduced *account-takeover* risk, but **not** exchange insolvency, hack of their cold storage, or seizure.

Many people use custodians for **trading float** and self-custody for **savings**.

nodes.title: Path summary — Custodial
nodes.body:
**Profile:** maximum convenience, institutional recovery, Lightning & trading — with counterparty, phishing, seizure, and insolvency risk.

**Profile notes:** high day-to-day ease and recoverability via support; lower resilience to systemic custodian failure; low personal operational burden.

Remember: educational framing only — not advice.

nodes.title: Federation
nodes.body:
A **federation** is a set of servers/operators that jointly custody or mint claims (e.g. federated e-cash / sidechain-style designs).

**Benefits**
- Exchange-like services; often Lightning
- **E-cash / confidential transactions** → stronger privacy than KYC exchanges
- Often secured by a **seed phrase** you hold for your federation wallet balance claim

**Can be phished.** Recovery/inheritance is **not** like resetting an exchange password — lose seeds and you may be stuck.

nodes.title: Federation — risks
nodes.body:
- **Hacks** of federation infrastructure
- **Collusion** among enough members to steal or censor
- **Government seizure** if the federation is **not jurisdictionally dispersed**
- Seed phishing / loss — recovery is not KYC-support-shaped
- Still a form of shared custody — not unilateral on-chain singlesig control of UTXOs (design-dependent)

nodes.title: Federation — mitigations
nodes.body:
- Prefer **jurisdictionally dispersed** operator sets
- Read threshold / membership / recovery documentation before sizing deposits
- Treat federation seeds with same OPSEC as Bitcoin seeds
- Don't put life savings in an experimental federation without understanding failure modes

nodes.title: Federation — hardened choice
nodes.body: You've improved legal-dispersion and operational awareness. Residual risk: collusion, novel smart-contract/federation bugs, and seed loss.

nodes.title: Single-key hot wallet
nodes.body:
A **hot wallet** keeps keys on an internet-connected phone or computer.

**Benefits:** easy spending, many apps, decent privacy vs KYC exchanges if used carefully.
**Recovery** depends entirely on **backups / seed handling**.
**Risk:** malware, clipboard hijack, fake apps, seed phishing.

choices.label: How will you create the seed?

nodes.title: Hot wallet — practical hardening
nodes.body: Even hardened, a hot single-sig remains exposed to OS malware. Common pattern: **hot wallet for spending**, cold/hardware for savings.

nodes.title: Path summary — Single-sig hot wallet
nodes.body: **Profile:** convenient daily spend, better privacy than exchanges, but malware and seed-handling dominate risk. Recovery = your backups.

nodes.title: Single-key hardware wallet
nodes.body:
A dedicated device holds keys and signs offline (USB/QR/NFC). The computer sees PSBTs/xpubs, not the seed (if used correctly).

**Benefits:** strong phishing resistance for signing; clear UX for address verification.
**Still single-sig:** one seed still rules all.
**Supply chain & seed generation** matter enormously.

choices.label: Generate seed on / for the device

nodes.title: Hardware supply chain
nodes.body:
- Buy from manufacturer or highly trusted reseller
- Inspect **tamper-evident** packaging
- Verify firmware signatures on first use
- Prefer devices that accept **user entropy**
- Know that **same-vendor multisig ≠ independence**

nodes.title: Hardware wallet ready
nodes.body: Device provenance improved. Next risks are seed ceremony quality, backup durability, and single-key failure.

nodes.title: Path summary — Single-sig cold / hardware
nodes.body: **Profile:** strong day-to-day security vs malware if air-gapped/hardware signing is done right; complexity rises; recoverability hinges on backups & inheritance docs. Single seed remains a single point of failure.

nodes.title: Air-gapped / cold storage
nodes.body:
Keys live on a device that **never** connects to the internet. Transactions move via QR, SD card, or USB as PSBTs.

**Tradeoff:** stronger malware resistance; higher operational burden; less day-to-day ease.
Air-gaps fail when people "just quickly" plug in Wi‑Fi to install software.

nodes.title: Air-gapped phone
nodes.body:
A dedicated phone flashed offline (or kept airplane-mode forever) can run a signing wallet.

**Vulnerabilities:** breaking air-gap to install apps; malicious APKs; cameras/mics; assuming airplane mode = safe while Bluetooth/NFC still on.
**Mitigations:** USB ferry of verified APKs; disable radios in hardware if possible; verify addresses on-device.

nodes.title: Air-gapped PC / live OS
nodes.body:
Examples: Tails-like live USB, dedicated laptop with networking physically removed.

**Note:** Electrum on Tails is popular for learning, but **Electrum does not generate BIP39 seeds** — restore incompatibility with BIP39 hardware wallets.

nodes.title: Air-gap operationally hardened
nodes.body: You've treated software transport as part of the threat model. Still verify every receive address on the offline screen before sharing it online.

nodes.title: Multisignature
nodes.body:
**Multisig** requires *m-of-n* keys to spend (e.g. 2-of-3). No single seed loss or theft necessarily loses funds.

**Benefits:** removes single point of failure; flexible recovery designs.
**Costs:** backup of *each* key + descriptor/output script; wallet software complexity; fee/UX overhead.

nodes.title: Same-vendor multisig ≠ independent
nodes.body:
If all signers share firmware, RNG, and supply chain, **one vendor bug can hit your threshold**.

Historical lesson: firmware RNG defects are not fixed for existing seeds by updating — **migrate**. Prefer multi-vendor so one bug can't satisfy *m*.

nodes.title: Multi-vendor multisig
nodes.body: Distinct manufacturers, purchase channels, and entropy sources. Export and backup the **wallet descriptor** (or equivalent) — without it, keys alone may not help.

nodes.title: Distributed multisignature
nodes.body:
Keys (or seed backups) live in **different locations** — home, office, safe deposit, relatives — so fire/theft at one site doesn't hit threshold.

Still ensure you can assemble *m* keys when you need to spend or rotate.

nodes.title: Multisig with multiple independent parties
nodes.body:
Co-signers are different people/orgs (spouse, attorney, collaborative-custody firm, friend).

**Pros:** inheritance & travel resilience.
**Cons:** collusion/coercion; a co-sign **service** can become custodian-like if they can refuse signatures.

nodes.title: Collaborative custody / key agent
nodes.body:
A firm holds one key and co-signs under policy (travel rule, fraud checks, inheritance).

Useful — but you've reintroduced **counterparty** and policy risk for that key. Keep *m* such that you can still spend if the firm disappears (e.g. 2-of-3 where you hold 2).

nodes.title: Peer multi-party multisig
nodes.body: Social recovery style: trusted humans hold keys. Document legal/practical expectations; practice a recovery drill.

nodes.title: Backing up multisig
nodes.body: Backup **each seed**, the **descriptor**/configuration, derivation paths, and a written recovery playbook. Test restoring on a spare device with a tiny amount first.

nodes.title: Path summary — Multisig
nodes.body: **Profile:** higher security against single theft/loss; complexity and coordination cost rise. Independence (vendors, locations, people) is the whole point — same-vendor stacks undermine it.

nodes.title: High-security protocols (Glacier-style)
nodes.body:
**Glacier**-style protocols use dual permanently offline computers, detailed printed checklists, dice entropy, and meticulous verification for cold storage.

**Security:** among the highest for single-org self-custody.
**Complexity:** very high — human error becomes the dominant residual risk.
**Recoverability:** only as good as your metal backups + written procedures for heirs.

nodes.title: Glacier-style ceremony outline
nodes.body:
1. Two air-gapped machines (or one + hardware), never networked
2. Dice / verified entropy → BIP39 words on paper
3. Checksum verification offline
4. Test receive addresses; fund only after dual verification
5. Metal backup; geographic diversity; inheritance sealed instructions

Practice with **throwaway** entropy first.

nodes.title: Path summary — Glacier-style
nodes.body: **Profile:** maximum procedural security, minimum convenience, high complexity. Best for infrequent-move cold storage when the operator will actually maintain the discipline.

nodes.title: Generating a seed phrase
nodes.body:
A BIP39 seed (12 or 24 words) encodes entropy + checksum. **How** you generate it dominates long-term security.

**Option 1:** A device generates the seed (hardware, air-gapped phone, Tails/Electrum, brain wallet).
**Option 2:** You generate the first 11/23 words (dice, cards, lottery…) then compute the checksum word offline.

nodes.title: Device-generated seed
nodes.body: Choose how the device creates entropy:

nodes.title: TailsOS + Electrum
nodes.body:
Electrum is powerful on an amnesic OS, but it **does not generate BIP39** mnemonics. Seeds won't restore into most hardware wallets expecting BIP39.

Use Electrum when you plan to stay in the Electrum ecosystem — or pick BIP39 tooling for interoperability.

nodes.title: Hardware wallet seed generation
nodes.body:
**Vulnerabilities**
- Unsafe seed-gen software (rogue employee / malicious provider)
- Compromised supply chain
- Insufficient entropy / firmware RNG defects
- Firmware update **does not** fix existing weak seeds — migrate funds

**Mitigations**
- Tamper-evident seal checks
- Provide your own entropy (often **50–100 dice rolls / coin flips / key mashing** per device docs)

nodes.title: User entropy on hardware — follow-on risks
nodes.body:
Even with dice, residual issues:

- Instructions not followed → not enough entropy
- Device **ignores** your entropy
- Audit missed bugs; software changed after audit
- Audited source ≠ built/signed binary
- Forced upgrades

**Mitigations:** follow provider instructions; audit/trust audited code; council of expert auditors; run exactly audited version; verify signatures; diversify vendors (especially in multisig).

nodes.title: Trusting device RNG alone
nodes.body:
Historically, firmware RNG bugs have produced weak seeds. If a defect is announced: **move funds to a newly generated seed** — updating firmware is not enough.

Prefer verifiable user entropy and multi-vendor multisig so one vendor bug can't hit threshold.

nodes.title: Air-gapped phone seed generation
nodes.body:
Generate BIP39 on a phone that never leaves airplane mode / has radios disabled.

Verify the APK signature before install (via USB ferry). After generation, write the seed offline; confirm restore produces the same first address.

choices.label: Verified APK + written seed + restore test

nodes.title: Brain wallet
nodes.body: Memorized passphrases as seeds are **routinely brute-forced**. Do not use for real funds. Educational dead-end.

choices.label: Choose a real entropy method instead

nodes.title: Air-gapped PC — BIP39 tooling
nodes.body: Use a verified live OS or dedicated machine. Ferry software via USB; compute or generate BIP39 offline; never reconnect.

nodes.title: You generate first 11/23 words
nodes.body: Physical entropy → BIP39 wordlist mapping. Then compute the **checksum (last) word** with air-gapped tooling.

nodes.title: Dice methods
nodes.body:
Common approach: 6-sided dice with a mapping table (e.g. patterns using rolls limited to 1–4 plus heads/tails-style tables) to pick words uniformly.

**Vulnerabilities**
- Rolling multiple dice then **sorting** biases word choice
- Biased physical dice (usually small entropy loss)
- Unsafe / incorrect instructions

**Mitigations:** follow instructions; casino/tested dice; trustworthy guides; never sort multi-die outcomes before mapping.

choices.label: Casino dice + trusted table + no sorting

nodes.title: Homegrown randomness → word mapping
nodes.body: Easy to introduce **modular bias** or off-by-one errors. Prefer established tables (diceware-style BIP39 mappings) over inventing encodings.

choices.label: Use a reviewed dice table instead

nodes.title: Playing cards / Seedpicker Solitaire
nodes.body: Shuffled cards can provide entropy if the shuffle is thorough and the mapping is unbiased. Seedpicker-style solitaire procedures exist in the community — use a **reviewed** guide; do math on paper.

nodes.title: Word lottery
nodes.body: Drawing words from a physical BIP39 word list can work if draws are with proper replacement/ordering rules so entropy is uniform — easy to get wrong. Prefer dice with known math.

nodes.title: Seed ceremony OPSEC
nodes.body:
Cross-cutting rules:

- **Writing intermediate math on an internet device** → use pencil/paper only
- **Speaking words** → never speak the seed (home audio / phones)
- **Cameras** → ensure no cameras (cover webcams; phones out)

nodes.title: Last word (checksum)
nodes.body:
BIP39's final word encodes a checksum over the entropy. Computing it needs correct software.

**Options:** Bitcoin hardware, air-gapped phone, air-gapped PC.

**Vulnerabilities:** wrong CLI; breaking air-gap to install software; checksum mismatch vs what you wrote; address check uses different derivation path.

**Mitigations:** trustworthy CLI guide; USB ferry; reload seed twice and confirm same address; write software+version+derivation path; load xpub on online watcher and match offline address.

nodes.title: After seed creation
nodes.body:
Before sending serious value:

1. Restore from backup on a second session/device
2. Confirm identical addresses (same script/path)
3. Optionally export xpub to a watch-only wallet
4. Decide on passphrase, geographic backups, inheritance notes

nodes.title: Getting the public key / xpub
nodes.body:
An **xpub** (extended public key) lets a watch-only wallet derive all receive/change addresses for an account **without** spending keys.

**How to export**
- **Phone:** wallet app export (hot — malware can steal xpub + poison UI)
- **Hardware:** QR / USB export of account xpub; confirm fingerprint on device
- **SD card / QR** from air-gapped signer
- **Air-gapped verify:** compare first addresses offline vs watcher

**Risks:** xpub leaks **privacy** (all addresses + history); watch-only malware can show **wrong** receive addresses (address poisoning). Always verify the address on the cold device screen.

nodes.title: Phone xpub export
nodes.body: Convenient but the phone can leak the xpub (privacy) and display attacker-controlled addresses. Prefer hardware confirmation for deposits above dust.

choices.label: Only use phone watcher; verify on cold device

nodes.title: Hardware xpub export
nodes.body: Export via QR or USB. Check the device's wallet fingerprint. On the online machine, import as watch-only and match address #0 with the hardware display.

nodes.title: Air-gapped xpub verify
nodes.body: Offline device shows address; online watcher (with xpub) should match. If they disagree, stop — derivation mismatch or malware.

nodes.title: Watch-only setup complete
nodes.body: You can monitor balances online without exposing spending keys. Treat the xpub as sensitive. For every receive, glance at the cold/hardware screen.

nodes.title: Backup, disasters & inheritance
nodes.body:
**Physical theft** of seed backups, **fire/flood**, and **inheritance without clear instructions** destroy more coins than clever cryptography.

Also: never photograph seeds; metal > paper for fire; geographic diversity helps disasters but increases theft surface.

nodes.title: Physical backups
nodes.body:
- Stamp seeds into metal (or quality plates)
- Avoid single points of disaster
- Consider sealed tamper-evident bags
- Multisig can mean each location holds one key (not the whole)

nodes.title: Inheritance
nodes.body:
Heirs need a **playbook**: where materials are, which software/paths, whether a passphrase exists, who can help verify — **without** pasting the seed into a will that becomes public probate.

Practice a guided recovery with a trusted person using a **test** wallet first.

nodes.title: Backup posture improved
nodes.body: Recoverability is up. Re-test restores periodically — especially after software upgrades.

nodes.title: BIP39 passphrase (25th word)
nodes.body:
An optional passphrase creates a hidden wallet. Great for plausible deniability / extra secrecy — catastrophic if lost or untested.

**Rules:** backup separately from the seed; test recovery; record wallet fingerprint/xpub so you know you opened the right wallet.

choices.label: Use passphrase with separate backup + test

nodes.title: Signing & address verification
nodes.body:
Spend path risks:

- Malware-infected verifier shows **poisoned addresses**
- Fake support asks you to "re-enter seed to sync"
- Wrong derivation → sending to an address you don't control

**Habit:** verify full address (or verified QR) on hardware/air-gapped display; never type seeds into websites.

nodes.title: Signing hygiene adopted
nodes.body: Good. Combine with multisig if amounts warrant. Educational demo complete for this branch — explore other ladder rungs or recommended paths.
